I am a man of 50 years, farming rice here in North Central. This plot of mine, small as it is, feeds my family, so I must put fertilizer — without it the rice will not give good yield. I cannot afford too much, but I buy urea and NPK when the cooperative brings it, and I use the improved seed my neighbor shared last year because it gave better grain. I have no pump for irrigation, so I depend on the rain and the lowland moisture, and my wife and children will help me, but I must also hire some young men for transplanting and harvest time.
